chunks: From him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who gives a specific measure (aqfizah) of wheat to be ground, paying the miller with dirhams. When the miller finished grinding, he paid the dirhams and gave back one qafiz from the wheat. This was a thing they had agreed upon between themselves. The Imam said: 'There is no harm in it, even if he did not explicitly urge him to do so.'
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to pay a miller with cash and receive a fixed amount of flour in return?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* validates the *Sulh* (amicable settlement) mechanism in commercial transactions, illustrating how mutual agreement (*istiqlah*) can legitimize exchanging a specific quantity of grain for milling services paid in cash and kind. It highlights the Shia juristic principle that flexibility in contract terms is permissible provided there is no ambiguity (*gharar*) or coercion, reflecting the practical economic needs of the early Islamic community. The Imam’s confirmation underscores that the essence of the agreement lies in the parties' consent rather than rigid formalities.
